MOB_QUIRKS: Attack in coordinated packs and retreat to regroup when one falls.
Explode on death. Do not melee the last one in a group.
Will trade contraband for shiny objects if you approach unarmed.
Blind, but hunt by sound. Silence works better than stealth.
Territorial and slow. Easy to outrun, nearly impossible to outfight in their lair.
Cowardly alone, murderous in groups of four or more.
Cast a low-tier fear effect on their first hit.
Steal one item from inventory on a critical hit, then flee.
Spit a corrosive fluid that eats non-magical armor.
Feign death after taking 50% damage. Confirm the kill.
Follow a shrieking alpha; kill the alpha and the rest scatter.
Regenerate slowly unless the wound is burned.
Hoard trash and build barricades across chokepoints.
Distracted by food. A dropped ration buys thirty seconds.
Aggressive toward anyone carrying a lit flame.
Set crude tripwire traps at every intersection in their territory.
Carry rusted weapons that inflict a lingering disease debuff.
Pathologically drawn to safe room doors. Expect a welcoming party when you leave.
Nocturnal by floor-clock; halve their numbers during the floor's 'day' cycle.
Mistake anyone in a hat for their leader. Briefly.
SYSTEM_DESC: Imagine {a} {b} that has been told, repeatedly and by everyone, that it is not enough. Now give it a weapon.
The {noun} of this neighborhood have formed a cooperative. The cooperative has one rule, and it is about you.
They are {adj_l}. They are {noun_l}. They are exactly as bad as that sounds.
Each of these {noun_l} was once a promising young {noun_sing}. Then they discovered crawlers.
Somebody in the writers' room really wanted {noun_l} on this floor. That person has since been reassigned. The {noun_l} remain.
Do not pet the {noun_l}. Do not feed the {noun_l}. Do not make eye contact with the {noun_l}. Honestly, just leave.
Not the strongest thing on this floor. Not the smartest. Definitely the most committed.
These come in bunches. Like bananas, if bananas hated you personally.
The System classifies these as 'low threat.' The System has never had to fight one in a hallway.
Picture {a} {b} with the specific energy of something that has nothing left to lose and never had much to begin with.
Every {noun_sing} on this floor shares one collective brain cell. Whoever is holding it is currently in charge.
Sponsored content: the {noun_l} of this neighborhood are brought to you by a company that has asked not to be named in connection with them.
Threat assessment: {adj_l}. Numbers: sufficient. Mercy: not a feature of this build.
They were {adj_l} before it was cool. They will be {adj_l} long after you are not anything.
The {noun_l} know they are on television. This has not improved their behavior.
Audience polling ranks these ninth in likability and second in kills. Make of that what you will.
{a} {b} is not, on paper, a serious problem. You will not be fighting one on paper.
A previous crawler described the {noun_l} as 'honestly kind of fine, actually.' That crawler is a dead crawler.
The {noun_l} have a hierarchy, a territory, and a long memory. You have already been added to the third one.
Management reminds crawlers that {noun_l} are a natural part of this ecosystem, and that complaints have been filed and ignored.
Studies confirm that running from {noun_l} triggers pursuit. Studies confirm that standing still also triggers pursuit. Studies are ongoing.
Do not be fooled by the fact that one of them is wearing a hat. It did not make the hat. It acquired the hat.
{a} {b} has roughly the survival instincts of a smoke alarm: loud, ignored, and somehow still going off at three in the morning.
This is what happens when you take a {noun_sing} and remove every reason it ever had to be reasonable.
BOSS_FORMS: {a_size} {size}-foot mass of fused {noun_l}, rolling as a single screaming unit
{a_size} gaunt, {size}-foot giant wearing the pelts of {noun_l} like a shawl
an obese, waist-deep-in-garbage matriarch of the local {noun_l}
a mechanical contraption piloted by an unknown number of {noun_l}
{a_size} {size}-foot centipede-thing with {noun_sing} heads grafted along its length
a floating, bloated sac that births {noun_l} when struck
a former crawler, long since turned, still wearing the remains of a uniform
a hive-mind swarm that takes a humanoid shape only when it wants to talk to you
a hulking {noun_sing} who has clearly been eating the other {noun_l}
{a_size} {size}-foot stone effigy animated by the collective spite of the {noun_l}

any: Immune to damage while any of its minions are alive in the chamber.
Splits into two smaller copies at 50% health. Kill both within a minute or it reforms.
Summons a wave of local mobs each time it loses a quarter of its health.
Only vulnerable from behind. Turns slowly.
Screams on a timer; the scream stuns anyone not behind cover.
Grabs and swallows a crawler; the swallowed crawler must deal damage from inside.
Drops the chamber's lights at 25% health. Bring your own.
Weak point is exposed only while it performs its charge attack.
Feeds on dropped items in the arena; a spilled inventory heals it.
Can be talked to. Cannot be reasoned with.
Bleeds an acid pool that grows as the fight drags on. Speed matters.
Fixates on the lowest-level crawler in the chamber.
Enrages when the floor timer crosses a whole hour.
Copies the last ability used against it, once, and uses it better.
Heals for every point of damage it deals. Burst it down or starve it out.
Counts hits, not damage. Every tenth hit staggers it regardless of size.
Cannot be hurt twice by the same weapon. Rotate, or bring friends.
Drops a loot box mid-fight; opening it during the fight applies a debuff.
Swaps places with a random crawler every thirty seconds.
Armour flakes where it is struck; the same spot takes more each time.
Regenerates in darkness, and will break the lights itself to get some.
Mirrors damage back at half value until its pauldrons are broken.
Marks one crawler; only that crawler's damage counts until the mark is passed.
Has two health bars. The second one fights nothing like the first.
Goes untargetable below half and hunts from the chamber walls.
Heals a tenth for every crawler who leaves the chamber.
Borrows one crawler's buffs for ten seconds at a time.
Gains a stack of armour each time a crawler uses a consumable.
Ignores the highest-level crawler entirely. Pride is the trap.
Knocks crawlers into the chamber's hazards rather than finishing them itself.
Eats corpses, mob or crawler, and grows a size each time.
Reflects all damage for five seconds after it roars. Learn the tell.
Shrugs off any single hit below a threshold. Chip damage does nothing.
Only takes full damage while it is standing in its own blood.
Cannot be hit while airborne, and spends half the fight airborne.
Charms a crawler each phase; break it by dealing damage to the charmed.
Locks the chamber at the first hit. It opens when one side is dead.
Detonates its minions rather than let them be killed.
Rewinds ten seconds of damage whenever a crawler dies.
Stacks a poison that only clears while the crawler stands perfectly still.
Pulls the air from the chamber in stages, with one breathing window per phase.
Its weak point moves each phase, and the System announces it sarcastically.
Draws a sponsor mid-fight, who drops a buff for whichever side is losing.
Plays to the crowd: takes half damage unless somebody is being flashy.
Calls a second boss in from a neighbouring chamber if the fight runs long.
Will not attack a crawler who is not looking at it.
Anchored to a totem elsewhere in the neighbourhood. Kill that first.
Will not start a fight it did not pick. A patient party can walk past.
Its minions resurrect it once, unless they are cleared first.
Immune while monologuing, and it monologues often.
Every interrupt strips a permanent stack of armour.
Every crawler it kills fights for it for the rest of the fight.
Takes double damage from the weapon that last killed something in this room.
Refuses to fight to a thin audience. It will wait, and heal while it waits.
Absorbs one damage type per phase, chosen at random, and is healed by it.
Moves faster the more health it loses, not slower.
Turns invisible below half, betrayed only by what it disturbs.
grand: The arena floor shifts every 30 seconds, funneling crawlers toward it.
Collapses a section of the chamber each phase until there is nowhere left to stand.
Floods the chamber from the floor up; the fight has to move higher each phase.
Fights in three chambers at once and has to be beaten in all of them.
Brings the ceiling down on a timer. Cover must be rebuilt between phases.
Summons a named lieutenant each phase, each with a gimmick of its own.
Reverses the chamber's gravity at every phase change.
Splits into four, one per corner, each with a quarter of its health and one ability.
Takes no damage until its three anchors elsewhere on the floor are destroyed.
Drags the party into a pocket arena; the way out opens when it dies.
Resets the fight to full health once, and remembers everything the party did.
The System sells live buffs to viewers. The crowd decides how hard this gets.
Feeds on the floor countdown: every hour that passes adds a phase.
Its death is broadcast floor-wide, and everything nearby comes to watch.

LOOT_THEMES: Goblin engineering: coal, gunpowder, crude mechanical parts, and the occasional working gadget.
Alchemical scraps: half-labeled vials, reagents, and glassware. Some of it is still potent.
Scavenged crawler gear: mismatched armor pieces, worn boots, and looted personal effects.
Butcher's bounty: hides, organs, teeth, and other crafting materials. Bring bags.
Contraband: narcotics, moonshine, counterfeit coin, and things you cannot legally carry on most planets.
Ritual junk: candles, bone charms, and low-tier cursed trinkets that mostly don't do anything.
Tools and hardware: hammers, chain, spikes, bolts. Nothing enchanted; everything useful.
Rations and consumables: preserved food, dubious water, bandages, and torches.
Textiles and vanity: cloaks, jewelry, cosmetics, and enchanted accessories of questionable taste.
Weapon scrap: broken blades, spear shafts, and arrowheads. Good for a crafter, dead weight for anyone else.
Paper trail: ledgers, maps, letters, and lore drops about this floor's storyline.
Trap components: tripwire, pressure plates, and reusable spring mechanisms.
Explosives: crude, unstable, and plentiful.
Pets and eggs: unhatched or infant versions of the local mob. Handle carefully.
Coin and bribes: small gold drops and items the local mobs value for trade.
Medical salvage: splints, sutures, and a half-used healing potion somebody clearly needed more.
Sponsor swag: branded tat nobody wants, except the sponsors are watching you take it.
Mining haul: ore, raw gems, and a pickaxe worn down to nothing.
Stage props: costumes, breakaway furniture, and a sword that is only a sword if you believe hard enough.
Kitchen stock: knives, oil, flour, and spices worth more than the knives.
Salvaged plumbing: pipe, valves, and enough lead to worry a healer.
Fishing kit: nets, line, hooks, and bait that is still moving.
Legal documents: deeds, writs, and one contract with a crawler's name already on it.
Lost luggage: suitcases from the surface, still packed for a holiday nobody took.
Office supplies: binders, stamps, and a stapler that does respectable damage.
Taxidermy: mounted heads of mobs from floors below this one.
Beast tack: saddles, muzzles, barding, and a bridle sized for nothing you want to meet.
Cult inventory: robes in four sizes, a ledger of dues, and a ceremonial knife that is just a knife.
Scrying junk: cracked mirrors, bowls, and one lens that shows a room you have not found.
Winter gear: furs, oil lamps, and boots two sizes too big.
Masonry: cut stone, mortar, and scaffold enough to wall something in.
Children's things: toys, chalk, a school satchel. Take the satchel.
Siege leftovers: bolts, shot, pitch, and half a trebuchet arm.
Barber-surgeon's case: razors, tongs, leeches, and an itemized bill for services.
Perfumery: oils, resins, and one scent the local mobs will follow for an hour.
Printing stock: type, ink, and a press plate for a wanted poster with a blank face.
Lockwork: picks, blanks, keys, and one key that fits nothing on this floor.
Gambling stock: cards, dice, chips, and a marker signed by someone who died owing.
Funeral supplies: shrouds, urns, coffin nails, and a discount for bulk.
Livestock feed: grain, salt licks, and whatever has been living in the grain.
Glassworks: panes, bottles, lenses, and a floor nobody should cross barefoot.
Signal gear: flares, horns, mirrors, and a whistle only the mobs can hear.
Rope and rigging: cable, pulleys, harness, and one knot nobody can undo.
Dyes and pigments: powders, brushes, and a red that stains for a week.
Quartermaster's error: forty of one item and none of anything else.
Confiscated goods: a shelf of things taken off the crawlers who came through first.
Botanical haul: cuttings, seeds, spores, and one plant that leans toward you.
Instrument cases: strings, drums, reeds, and a horn that buffs whoever can play it.
Timepieces: clocks, sandglasses, and one that runs backwards near the boss.
Bath house stock: soap, towels, oils, and the first hot water in days.
Scrapped automata: gears, servos, and a head that still tracks movement.
Religious relics: bones in boxes, mostly fake, one emphatically not.
Apiary: hives, smokers, wax, and bees with opinions.
Cartography: survey tools, blank vellum, and a map of this floor that is wrong on purpose.
Fireworks: display shells, fuses, and a launch tube. Loud, bright, a terrible idea indoors.
Hazard kit: masks, gloves, antidotes, and a warning label in a language nobody reads.
Mob wages: tally sticks, coin pouches, and a payroll list with names on it.
Dentistry: pliers, mirrors, a jar of teeth, and no anesthetic.
JANITOR_MECHANICS: Consume corpses; each corpse eaten raises them one level. Clear bodies or clear out.
Spawn in proportion to the local kill count. Big fights breed big swarms.
White-tagged until struck. Striking one aggroes every janitor in earshot.
Drag corpses to a central pit. Follow the drag marks and you'll find the pit. Don't.
Mutate after enough meals into a flying, aggressive adult form.
Ignore crawlers entirely unless a crawler is carrying a corpse or body part.
Sweep the tunnels on a cycle; be inside a safe room when you hear the chittering.
Dissolve loot left on corpses within an hour. Loot fast.
